richard-dare-s-venture-or-striking-out-f: Edward Stratemeyer, the man behind the Hardy Boys and Tom Swift, wrote dozens of such adventures for boys. Young Richard Dare leaves home to make his own way, facing hard work, sharp dealers, and honest chances in turn. Fast-moving and full of pluck, the story delivers exactly what its young readers wanted: a hero who earns his success.
the-history-of-thomas-ellwood-written-by: Thomas Ellwood, Milton's Quaker friend, tells his own tale of jail and faith in Stuart England. His plain, true book is a gem of Quaker writing and a live picture of the age. Honest, brave, and of real worth to history.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aloys-lutolf: This 1913 reference piece on Aloys Lutolf — a Swiss historian. Patricius Schlager notes his research. His pages lit the old Confederation. The entry honors his scholarship. A chronicler of the Alpine past. His volumes grace the Swiss libraries. His chronicle ends with the old republic.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arculf: A 1913 entry on Arculf — the Frankish pilgrim of the Holy Land. Thomas Walsh tells his seventh-century journey. Adamnan wrote down his tale. His map guided the medieval pilgrims. The wanderer who mapped Jerusalem. His voyage ended on Iona's shore.
